record.narrative: No prior ledger evidence exists, so iteration 1 registers a broad but tractable set of main-effect hypotheses spanning the outcome set. I prioritize outcomes with comparatively larger dispersion and/or more distinctive dependency distributions (outcome_014, outcome_006, outcome_001, outcome_011, outcome_008, outcome_013) while still covering additional CRISPR dependency scores. Exposures are restricted to measured binary or two-level categorical features with large enough cells for the 20-observation cell-count rule. Because predictor labels are opaque, the directional assignments are exploratory hypotheses about whether an exposure level behaves like a dependency-enhancing or dependency-reducing marker, not causal biological claims. For outcome_014 and outcome_006, which have less-negative mean scores, I register positive-direction hypotheses (exposure associated with weaker dependency, i.e., higher score). For most remaining rare or binary marker exposures, I register negative-direction hypotheses (exposure associated with stronger dependency, i.e., more negative score), and for the categorical feature_054 comparison I test whether level_002 has stronger dependency than level_001. All comparisons start unresolved. Later, large estimates, interval widths, and whether the effect size plausibly crosses the 10% relative-difference threshold will guide refinement, reversal, subgroup interaction testing, and optional validation.

I request all twelve registered discovery comparisons now. Each analysis is a mean_difference exposed minus comparator using Welch 95% intervals and requiring at least 20 observations in each comparison cell. These tests provide initial signed effect estimates, uncertainty intervals, and cell-count diagnostics for the broad set of predictor-outcome pairs registered in iteration 1. I am not changing any claim status at this stage because no evidence has been returned yet.

All twelve discovery comparisons were validly estimated and had adequate cell counts. None showed a statistically significant association: every 95% Welch interval crossed zero. I approximated the clinical benchmark as 10% of the absolute outcome mean because dependency scores are centered below zero. Under that benchmark, many original directional claims can be rejected as not reaching clinically meaningful magnitude: the upper confidence bound for the hypothesized direction was below roughly 10% for H2 through H5, H8, and H10 through H12. Several of these estimates were also opposite the registered direction, including H2, where feature_060=1 had a signed estimate of -0.0235 relative to the positive-direction claim; for the opposite dependency-enhancing direction, that point estimate is around 25% of the outcome_006 absolute mean, although the interval still crosses zero. Because the evidence is not significant and arose among 12 exploratory tests, I do not accept it, but I registered a reversed claim and follow-up generalization tests. For H1, H6, H7, and H9, the confidence intervals just touch or slightly exceed the approximate clinical threshold in the hypothesized direction, so I recorded them as unresolved rather than accepting any claim; they are not precise enough or large enough to support acceptance. I did not request independent validation because no candidate is compelling enough to justify a validation slot now; the stronger follow-up is to see whether the feature_060 reverse signal or untested categorical/binary comparisons replicate in the same dataset before spending validation. These are dataset associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

No independent validation results or response deadlines were delivered at this synthesis stage, so the accepted claim set is unchanged and no finding is upgraded to accepted based on validation. The first discovery scan is complete: all twelve initial comparisons had adequate cell counts and 95% Welch intervals that include zero. Using an approximate 10% relative-difference benchmark scaled to the absolute outcome mean, many registered main effects are negative or clinically unmeaningfully small; H2-H5, H8, and H10-H12 were therefore rejected. The main exception for follow-up is the reversed feature_060 contrast for outcome_006, registered as H13. R2 shows a signed estimate of +0.0235 for direction -1, i.e. a raw exposed-minus-comparator difference of about -0.0235, meaning feature_060=1 is associated with a more negative dependency score. That magnitude exceeds the approximate 10% threshold for outcome_006, but the interval crosses zero and the direction was post hoc after observing the opposite original claim, so this is an unresolved candidate rather than a supported finding. I closed H13 as a discovery analysis to avoid wasting a future analysis slot on an already tested comparison, while leaving it unresolved pending convergent evidence from H14-H25. The most informative next analysis is the active set now spanning feature_060 across correlated CRISPR dependency scores, feature_002 on other outcomes, untested categorical levels, and an interaction for outcome_006 by feature_034. Convergence in the same dataset, especially repeated dependency-enhancing signals with intervals crossing a clinically meaningful boundary, would justify validation; uniformly null or imprecise follow-up should lead to rejecting the candidate. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal effects or generalizable biological claims.

The strongest discovery signal so far is the reversed feature_060 contrast for outcome_006: relative to direction -1, R2 gives a signed estimate of +0.0235, corresponding to a raw exposed-minus-comparator score of about -0.0235 and suggesting stronger dependency in feature_060=1 samples. That raw effect is large relative to outcome_006's approximate 10% clinical benchmark (about 0.0093), but the interval crosses zero and the direction was observed post hoc. Therefore the next priority is to test whether the same feature_060 dependency-enhancing pattern appears in other CRISPR dependency scores rather than treating outcome_006 as a stand-alone finding. I register four refinements against feature_060 for outcome_002, outcome_003, outcome_010, and outcome_016, all with direction -1 and anticipated raw direction -1. These outcomes have absolute means around 0.25, so the 10% relative benchmark is roughly 0.025, close to the absolute contrast observed for outcome_006. With the already active feature_060 tests for outcome_005, outcome_012, outcome_004, outcome_014, and outcome_015, this gives a broad internal-consistency scan across about ten dependency scores. If several independent signed intervals are positive and at least one approaches or excludes the clinical threshold, validation would be worthwhile; if all are null or upper bounds remain below meaningful thresholds, the H13 candidate should be rejected. I keep H16 and H18 active because feature_002 is a balanced predictor and outcome_007/outcome_009 are untested for it, preserving some broad exploration. I defer H19-H22 only for the next analysis round because the registered categorical level pairs are less certain about cell counts and the feature_060 candidate is the higher-priority unresolved signal. These are in-dataset associations, not causal or generalizable conclusions.

I will analyze the active prioritized set exactly: feature_060 main effects across all currently active untested dependency outcomes (H14, H15, H17, H24, H25, H26, H27, H28, H29) and the outcome_006 interaction (H23), while keeping two broad feature_002 main effects in play (H16, H18). This maximizes information about the only current candidate signal, feature_060 dependency-enhancing association, and preserves some exploration of feature_002 without spending slots on deferred categorical contrasts. I am not changing statuses because no new evidence has yet been returned for these claims.

All twelve new discovery analyses are valid and have adequate cell counts, but none has a 95% interval excluding zero. Using an approximate clinical benchmark of 10% of the absolute outcome mean, feature_060 does not show a coherent dependency-enhancing main-effect pattern across the outcome panel. For outcome_005, outcome_012, outcome_004, outcome_015, outcome_002, outcome_003, outcome_010, and outcome_016, the signed confidence bounds in the hypothesized direction are below the approximate 10% threshold or the estimates are opposite the registered direction, so I reject H14, H15, H17, H25, H26, H27, H28, and H29 as not supported in this dataset. outcome_014 is an exception only because its absolute mean is small and the interval is wide; H24 remains unresolved but deferred. The feature_002 main effects on outcome_007 and outcome_009 are clinically unmeaningfully small, so H16 and H18 are rejected. The only candidate worth following is H23: the feature_060 by feature_034 interaction on outcome_006 has a large positive signed estimate (+0.0488, about 5x the approximate outcome_006 threshold), but its interval crosses zero and arose in an exploratory scan with substantial multiplicity. I do not accept it based on discovery alone, but it is the most promising eligible claim, so I request independent validation for H23. I also register direct follow-up comparisons for the subgroup variable and simple effects within feature_034=1 and feature_034=0 to characterize whether the interaction is real or an artifact of a null main effect. These remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

The independent validation for H23 is available and does not support the interaction candidate. R18 was a large positive discovery signed estimate for the feature_060 by feature_034 interaction on outcome_006 (+0.0488), with a CI crossing zero. The independent validation R25 gives the opposite signed estimate (-0.0146), with a very wide interval (-0.1122 to +0.0830) that also crosses zero. The validation is valid, cell counts are adequate, and the interval accounts for the maximum number of validation comparisons. Because the validation direction is opposite to the claim and neither discovery nor validation provides a statistically or clinically reliable positive interaction, I reject H23 as not supported in this dataset and close it. This failure, together with the inconsistent feature_060 main-effect panel (H14, H15, H17, H25-H29 rejected; H24 only imprecise; H13 unresolved but not convergent), closes the current feature_060 candidate track. No accepted findings are supported. Negative findings include the original feature_060 positive-direction claim H2, feature_002 main effects H3, H16, and H18, and many other initially tested binary contrasts H4, H5, H8, H10-H12, as well as H25-H29. Remaining unresolved uncertainty is limited to claims with intervals spanning clinically meaningful values but too imprecise to support acceptance, including H1, H6, H7, H9, H13, H24, and untested categorical contrasts H19-H22. The most informative next analysis is to run untested comparisons rather than retest old comparisons: activate H19-H22 and H30, and defer the H23-derived simple-effect comparisons H31 and H32. All conclusions remain in-dataset associations and do not establish causal effects or generalizable biology.

With the feature_060 candidate now failed validation, the next step should prioritize the already active categorical and balanced-binary contrasts (H19-H22, H30) and add a small set of high-value untested comparisons. First, I register refinements around unresolved upper-bound signals from H6, H7, and H9. These claims had adequate binary cell sizes and confidence bounds that just touched or exceeded the approximate 10% clinical threshold on their original outcomes, so testing the same predictors on related central dependency scores is a focused follow-up: feature_050 on outcome_004, feature_037 on outcome_016, and feature_045 on outcome_002. Each expects a raw exposed-minus-comparator negative difference, i.e. stronger dependency in the exposed level. Second, I register three rare-absence binary tests (feature_008, feature_047, and feature_023 exposed at 0 versus 1). These features have high prevalence, and the rare group remains large enough for Welch comparisons. The falsifiable hypothesis is that rare absence of the binary marker marks a state with stronger CRISPR dependency; alternatives are null or opposite association. Third, I register one balanced effect-modification test for feature_002 within feature_034 for outcome_005. This is broader than the failed H23 feature_060 interaction and tests whether a different predictor's dependency effect is modified by feature_034. These comparisons target clinically meaningful magnitudes while keeping conclusions limited to dataset-specific associations rather than causality or generalizability.

All twelve currently active claims are previously untested, so requesting them together maximizes new information in this analysis batch. The set includes broad categorical contrasts (H19-H22), the feature_034 main effect on outcome_006 (H30), focused outcome-consistency refinements around earlier upper-bound candidates (H33-H35), rare-absence high-prevalence binary markers (H36, H37, H39), and one balanced interaction for feature_002 modified by feature_034 (H38). These are prioritized over already tested or deferred comparisons because they test new predictors/contrast types and avoid reusing evidence from claims already assessed or rejected. No statuses are changed at this stage because no new evidence has been returned yet for these claims.

All twelve newly analyzed claims are valid, have adequate cell counts, and use the pre-specified signed direction. I used approximate 10% clinical benchmarks based on absolute outcome means: about 0.025 for most central dependency scores, about 0.0093 for outcome_006, and about 0.027 for outcome_013. Most new effects are not clinically or statistically supported. H21, H22, H33, H34, H35, and H38 are rejected: their intervals either do not reach the relevant clinical threshold or the signed estimate is opposite the hypothesized direction with no meaningful evidence in the registered direction. H30 is rejected for the directional hypothesis on outcome_006: feature_034=1 versus 0 shows a small opposite signed estimate, even though the interval is wide enough to include positive values. H19, H20, and H36 are left unresolved but deferred: their signed estimates are small and intervals cross zero, with upper bounds only modestly above the approximate threshold, so they do not justify validation or active follow-up. The only near candidates are the rare-absence binary markers H37 and H39. H37 has a signed estimate of +0.0253, about 9.4% of outcome_013's absolute mean, close to the clinical threshold, with a CI from -0.0016 to 0.0522. H39 has a signed estimate of +0.0232, about 9.1% of outcome_009's absolute mean, with a CI from -0.0023 to 0.0488. Neither discovery interval excludes zero, and neither point estimate itself reaches 10%, so I do not accept either on discovery evidence. However, both are near statistical and clinical relevance and could be real but noisy associations. I request independent validation for H37 because it is closest to the clinical threshold and closest to excluding zero. I keep H37 and H39 active and register cross-outcome follow-up tests for both markers to assess internal consistency. These remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

Independent validation for H37 is available. In the discovery sample (R35), feature_047=0 versus 1 on outcome_013 had a signed estimate +0.0253, approximately 9.4% of the absolute mean outcome_013 score, with a 95% interval of -0.0016 to +0.0522. In the independent validation sample (R38), the signed estimate was +0.0301, approximately 11.2% of the absolute outcome_013 mean, with a validation-adjusted interval of -0.0095 to +0.0696. Both estimates are in the claimed direction, and the validation point estimate exceeds the approximate 10% clinical threshold. Because discovery and independent validation are concordant and the effect size is near or above the clinically meaningful threshold, I accept H37 as a dataset-specific association between rare absence of feature_047 and stronger outcome_013 CRISPR dependency. However, both intervals include zero and the validation interval is wide because of the maximum-validation adjustment, so the estimate remains imprecise and the association should not be interpreted causally or as generalizable. I keep H37 active while cross-outcome consistency is tested. H39 remains unresolved and active pending its own validation or consistency evidence. The feature_060 interaction track and many earlier main-effect contrasts remain rejected/closed. The next priority is internal consistency for the two rare-absence marker candidates: feature_047 and feature_023. H40 and H41 were already registered for these cross-outcome checks, and I register additional follow-up tests on central dependency outcomes to determine whether these markers show repeated associations or whether H37 is an outcome-specific finding.

The highest-value follow-up is to map the two rare-absence binary markers across the remaining central CRISPR dependency outcomes. For feature_047, H37 is accepted as a dataset-specific association for outcome_013; testing outcome_004, outcome_010, and outcome_011 asks whether rare absence of feature_047 reflects a broader dependency-enhancing state or only an outcome_013-specific association. For feature_023, H39 is near the clinical threshold on outcome_009 but not validated; testing outcome_012, outcome_004, and outcome_010 tests internal consistency before requesting validation. Each proposal uses exposed=0 versus comparator=1, with direction -1 because the hypothesis is that absence is associated with a more negative, i.e. stronger, dependency score. Alternative outcomes include null or opposite associations. These comparisons have adequate rare-group counts and remain dataset-specific association tests, not causal or generalizable claims.

No claims are currently due for assessment, and no status changes are warranted before these new analyses. The highest-value next analyses are exactly the twelve untested active marker-consistency comparisons H40 through H51. These map rare absence of feature_047 and feature_023 across central CRISPR dependency outcomes, after the accepted feature_047 outcome_013 finding and the near-threshold feature_023 outcome_009 signal. I am not requesting H39 again because it already has discovery evidence; re-running it would reuse the same data and add no new sample. The selected set tests whether each marker has broad association or is outcome-specific, using the same direction convention: exposed=0 versus comparator=1, direction -1, so positive returned estimates indicate stronger dependency when the marker is absent.

All newly delivered comparisons are valid, have adequate cell counts, and use the registered signed direction: positive estimates indicate that rare absence of the marker is associated with a more negative, i.e. stronger, CRISPR dependency score. I compared each point estimate and confidence bound with approximate 10% clinical thresholds based on the absolute outcome means. The feature_047 consistency panel largely contradicts a broad marker hypothesis: after the accepted outcome_013 association, feature_047=0 versus 1 is small or opposite on outcome_009, outcome_012, outcome_005, outcome_004, and outcome_011, with most upper bounds below the 10% threshold. outcome_010 has a tiny positive estimate and an upper bound just crossing threshold, but the point is far below clinical relevance, so it is left unresolved only at low priority. Thus feature_047 appears best described as outcome_013-specific within this dataset rather than a broad dependency-enhancing marker. The feature_023 panel is also inconsistent with a broad absent-marker hypothesis: several outcomes show opposite signed estimates or upper bounds below threshold. outcome_015 and outcome_004 have small positive estimates whose confidence intervals permit clinically meaningful values, but the point estimates are only about 3-4%, so they remain unresolved but deferred rather than active. The key candidate is H39, outcome_009, which has a discovery signed estimate of +0.0232, approximately 9.1%, close to the clinical threshold and analogous in precision and effect magnitude to H37 before its positive validation. Because the cross-outcome feature_023 panel does not support a broad marker effect, validation of H39 is useful only as a targeted test of whether feature_023 is associated with an outcome_009-specific dependency difference. I request independent validation for H39, keep it active, close the completed feature_047 consistency investigation while retaining accepted H37, and close or defer the feature_023 cross-outcome comparisons that lack supportive evidence.

Current synthesis: the strongest evidence is still H37. In the supplied dataset, rare absence of feature_047 (exposed=0) is associated with stronger outcome_013 CRISPR dependency than feature_047=1: discovery signed estimate +0.0253, about 9.4 percent of the absolute mean score, and independent validation signed estimate +0.0301, about 11.2 percent. The validation point estimate exceeds the approximate 10 percent clinical threshold and the direction is concordant, supporting a dataset-specific association, but both intervals include zero and the validation interval is wide after maximum-validation adjustment, so the estimate is imprecise and should not be interpreted causally or as generalizable. The feature_047 cross-outcome panel does not support a broad marker effect: H40, H42, H43, H46, and H48 are rejected, and H47 is only a low-priority unresolved candidate because its point estimate is tiny despite an upper confidence bound near threshold. The feature_023 outcome_009 candidate H39 now has independent validation and fails to support a clinically meaningful association. Its discovery signed estimate was +0.0232, about 9.1 percent, and the independent validation estimate was lower at +0.0187, about 7.3 percent, with intervals crossing zero and not excluding zero in the validation. I therefore reject and close H39 as not supported for a clinically meaningful difference. H23 is also rejected after validation: the discovery signed interaction estimate on outcome_006 was large but uncertain, while the independent validation estimate was opposite the claimed direction and equally uncertain, so there is no support for that interaction. Other broad negative or weak results remain largely closed or deferred. The most informative next analysis is to complete the feature_047 specificity scan on the remaining untested dependency outcomes. If those new comparisons remain small, the conclusion strengthens that feature_047 is an outcome_013-specific dataset association rather than a broad dependency-enhancing marker. If any remaining outcome shows a near-10 percent signed association, that comparison should become the next focused validation target.

The highest-value active track remains defining the scope of the accepted feature_047-outcome_013 association. H37 is supported as a dataset-specific association: rare absence of feature_047 is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency, with signed discovery estimate +0.0253 and independent validation estimate +0.0301. Because outcome_013 has an absolute mean of about 0.269, an approximately 10 percent relative difference corresponds to a signed absolute difference near +0.027. The nine already registered comparisons H52-H60 ask whether this marker effect extends to other dependency outcomes. The three new proposals add focused subgroup refinements of H37 using common, balanced binary strata feature_034=1, feature_060=1, and feature_002=1. These strata are scientifically useful because they have adequate overlap with the rare feature_047-absent group, and they test whether the accepted association is preserved across plausible biological contexts or is limited to the full eligible population. The claimed direction is negative raw exposed-minus-comparator, i.e. signed positive estimates indicate stronger dependency when feature_047 is absent. The anticipated direction is also negative because a plausible null is that the accepted effect is context-independent across these common strata. Key alternatives are attenuation or null in one or more strata, an opposite-direction association suggesting effect modification, or a subgroup effect that is much smaller than the clinical threshold. Together with H52-H60, these give a 12-comparison panel that can either broaden feature_047 into a more specific outcome-subgroup claim or strengthen the conclusion that it is primarily an outcome_013-specific dataset association. No validation is requested now; validation should be reserved for a subgroup or outcome result that is near or above threshold with a direction supported by the new panel.

No claims are currently due for assessment and no existing claim should be reassessed before the new active panel is tested. The highest-value analyses are the twelve currently active, untested comparisons H52-H63. This set completes the feature_047 scope investigation that follows from accepted H37. H52-H60 test whether rare absence of feature_047 is associated with stronger dependency on the remaining major CRISPR dependency outcomes beyond outcome_013, including outcomes with different absolute means and therefore different absolute 10% clinical thresholds. H61-H63 directly refine the accepted outcome_013 association in three common balanced binary strata: feature_034=1, feature_060=1, and feature_002=1. All comparisons use feature_047=0 as exposed and feature_047=1 as comparator with direction -1, so returned positive estimates represent stronger dependency when feature_047 is absent. If the cross-outcome estimates remain small or opposite while the direct outcome_013 subgroup estimates remain positive and near or above the relevant thresholds, the evidence will support an outcome_013-specific dataset association. If one cross-outcome estimate is clinically meaningful, or if a subgroup estimate strongly diverges from H37, that specific comparison can become the next targeted validation candidate. Re-running older claims with existing evidence would add no new sample, so I am not selecting them.

All twelve new results are valid, have adequate cell counts, and use the registered signed direction: positive estimates mean that feature_047 absence is associated with stronger dependency for the tested outcome. The cross-outcome feature_047 panel mostly strengthens outcome_013 specificity. H52, H53, H56, H57, and H59 are rejected for the original stronger-dependency-when-feature_047-absent claim. H52, H53, H56, and H59 have upper bounds below the approximate 10% absolute-mean threshold, and H57 has a negative signed estimate with a confidence interval below zero, indicating the opposite direction rather than the claimed association. H57 is notable as a post-hoc opposite-direction candidate: its magnitude is near the 10% threshold for outcome_008, so I registered a reversed comparison as a new hypothesis for later analysis rather than accepting it from a post-hoc scan. H54, H55, H58, H60, H61, and H63 remain unresolved but deferred: their point estimates are small or opposite, and the remaining uncertainty mainly comes from wide intervals that merely include clinically meaningful values. I did not validate these low-priority unresolved candidates. The one active candidate is H62, outcome_013 within feature_060=1. Its signed estimate is +0.0481, about 17.9% of the absolute outcome_013 mean; the discovery confidence interval excludes zero but its lower bound (+0.0100) is still below the 10% threshold. Because this is a subgroup comparison selected from a 12-test panel, multiplicity and confounding/correlation with other features remain plausible competing explanations. Independent validation is therefore useful to test whether the strong outcome_013 association is genuinely preserved in the feature_060=1 stratum. I request validation for H62. No causal or external generalizability claim is being made.

The new validation changes the subgroup interpretation substantially. H37 remains the only feature_047 association supported across discovery and independent validation. For outcome_013, feature_047 absent versus present gives signed discovery estimate +0.0253 and signed validation estimate +0.0301, relative to an absolute mean score of about 0.269; these correspond to approximately 9.4% and 11.2% stronger dependency in the absent group. The validation point exceeds the approximate 10% threshold and the two estimates are direction-concordant, so I accept H37 as a dataset-specific association. However, both intervals include zero and the validation interval is wide after maximum-validation adjustment, so the claim should remain imprecise and noncausal rather than strong or generalizable. H62 is now rejected. Its discovery subgroup estimate within feature_060=1 was unexpectedly large at +0.0481, about 17.9% of the outcome_013 mean, but independent validation reversed to -0.0051 with an interval crossing zero and excluding clinically meaningful positive values in the claimed direction. This is strong evidence that the feature_060=1 subgroup effect is not robust and likely reflected selection/multiplicity after testing multiple strata. H62 failure does not overturn H37, because H37 was supported in the full population by independent validation, but it cautions against inferring stronger marker effects in any particular stratum. The most informative next analysis is validation of H64, the reversed outcome_008 claim suggested by H57: feature_047 present versus absent was associated with signed +0.0282, essentially at the 10% threshold and with a discovery interval excluding zero. Because that direction was discovered post hoc after the original absent-marker claim failed, independent validation is needed before accepting it. Other feature_047 subgroup candidates H61 and H63 should remain deferred at low priority, as their discovery estimates are below threshold and H62's failure reduces confidence in subgroup refinements.

No claims are due for assessment. The main registered discovery that should be prioritized for independent validation is H64: feature_047 present versus absent in outcome_008 has a signed discovery estimate of +0.0282, approximately 10% of the absolute outcome_008 mean, with a discovery interval excluding zero. Because this direction was discovered after the original absent-marker claim failed, it must be treated as post hoc and confirmed by validation. In addition to H64, I registered two focused feature_047 reversal candidates. The original absent-marker tests for outcome_006 and outcome_014 were rejected for the absent-stronger hypothesis, but their raw opposite-direction magnitudes were clinically meaningful relative to the small absolute means of these outcomes: about +0.0149 for outcome_006, about 16% of its absolute mean, and +0.0122 for outcome_014, about 13% of its absolute mean. I therefore registered present-versus-absent claims for outcome_006 and outcome_014, with anticipated raw negative differences, to test whether feature_047 presence marks stronger dependency in these low-mean outcomes as well as in outcome_008. If these reversed claims remain null or opposite, H64 will look more like an isolated post hoc finding rather than a coherent bidirectional feature_047 pattern.  I also registered a limited replication panel around the accepted outcome_013 association and candidate outcome_008 association. The goal is not broad subgroup mining, but to ask whether a broader predictor pattern exists: markers that behave like feature_047 should show either absent/alternative-state stronger dependency for outcome_013 or present/alternative-state stronger dependency for outcome_008. I selected predictors with adequate overlap and enough sample size: feature_063 level_002 versus level_001, feature_045, and feature_008. For each predictor I registered one outcome_013 and one outcome_008 comparison in the hypothesized direction. This allows discovery of independent associations while keeping the search tied to the two outcomes where feature_047 has produced signals. Key alternatives are null for all new predictors, an outcome-specific association with feature_047 only, or a reproducible marker pattern that may deserve validation. No causal or external generalizability claims are made; new near-threshold results should still be validated before acceptance.

No claims are due for assessment. I will run the six currently active, untested comparisons H67-H72. This is the highest-value focused follow-up to accepted H37 and post-hoc H64 candidate: it tests whether predictors with adequate sample overlap show the same conceptual direction as feature_047. Specifically, H67, H69, and H71 test whether an alternative or absent marker state is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency (returned positive estimates support the registered claim), while H68, H70, and H72 test whether an alternative or present marker state is associated with stronger outcome_008 dependency (the opposite-direction pattern suggested by the reversed feature_047 result). I selected feature_063 level_002 versus level_001, feature_045, and feature_008 because they are pre-registered active hypotheses with adequate cell sizes or binary frequency and can test whether the feature_047 pattern is isolated or part of a broader marker pattern. The approximate 10% absolute-mean thresholds are about 0.0269 for outcome_013 and 0.0282 for outcome_008, so results near those values will be treated as clinically meaningful candidate discoveries only if supported by coherent uncertainty. I am not re-running H64-H66 because they already have signed discovery evidence from their parent tests and re-running would not add a new sample. I am also leaving H31 and H32 deferred: they test direct feature_060 main effects within feature_034 strata for outcome_006, but the corresponding interaction H23 failed independent validation and feature_060 effects have generally been weak, so these are lower priority than the predictor-pattern panel. All returned estimates are already signed to the registered direction; positive values support stronger dependency in the hypothesized exposed/alternative/absent group for the registered hypothesis.

The six new predictor-panel results are valid and adequately powered in every cell. Positive signed estimates support stronger dependency in the registered exposed/alternative/absent state. For outcome_013, feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 (H67) is small (+0.0029) and its upper bound is below the approximate 10% absolute-mean threshold (~0.0269), so I reject it. feature_045 absent versus present (H69) is opposite the claimed direction and its upper bound is far below threshold; I reject it. feature_008 absent versus present (H71) has a small point estimate (+0.0101) but an upper bound above threshold, so I leave it unresolved but deferred: the evidence is too weak to prioritize. For outcome_008, feature_063 (H68) is small (+0.0077) but its upper bound just crosses the approximate 10% threshold (~0.0282), so I leave it unresolved/deferred rather than accept it. feature_045 present versus absent (H70) is opposite the claimed direction and below threshold, so I reject it. The one substantive candidate is H72: feature_008 present versus absent is associated with a signed estimate of +0.0322, about 11.4% of the absolute outcome_008 mean, and the discovery interval excludes zero. However, the lower bound is far below the clinical threshold and the interval remains wide. Because H72 was selected from a six-test panel and may be confounded by correlated marker features, I do not accept it yet; I request independent validation to determine whether the direction and magnitude are robust. No causal or external generalizability claim is made.

The new validation results close several candidate associations. H72 was the strongest new candidate: feature_008 present versus absent was associated with a signed discovery estimate of +0.0322 for outcome_008, about 11.4% of the absolute outcome_008 mean and above the approximate 10% clinical threshold. However, independent validation reversed the sign to -0.0256, with an adjusted interval from -0.0730 to +0.0218. This provides direct evidence that the discovery result was not robust, likely false-positive selection or confounding among correlated marker features. I therefore reject H72 and close it. H39 has a response deadline. Its discovery estimate (+0.0232) and validation estimate (+0.0187) are directionally positive for feature_023 absent versus present on outcome_009, but both are below the approximate 10% absolute-mean threshold (~0.0256) and their intervals include zero. Thus the claim is not supported at the clinically meaningful magnitude, and I keep it rejected. H42 was validated as a cross-outcome feature_047 check: the validation point estimate is near zero (+0.0001), with an interval of -0.0303 to +0.0305. This is not clinically meaningful and confirms that feature_047 absence does not produce a broad outcome_012 association. Together, these validations strengthen the conclusion that the currently accepted H37 outcome_013 association is relatively outcome-specific rather than part of a broad marker pattern. The most important unresolved candidate is now H64: feature_047 present versus absent for outcome_008. Its discovery evidence is direction-coherent at the clinical threshold (signed +0.0282, about 10%), but it was generated post hoc after the original absent-marker outcome_008 claim failed, so it should not be accepted without independent validation. I registered a small new marker panel for outcome_013 and outcome_008 using feature_042, feature_021, and feature_037 to test whether any other binary markers reproduce either the accepted outcome_013 absent-marker direction or the candidate outcome_008 present-marker direction. If these remain null or opposite, H37 becomes even more isolated; if a new predictor crosses the threshold with coherent uncertainty, it becomes a better validation candidate. No causal or external generalizability claim is made.

No claims are due for evidence assessment. The accepted finding remains H37: in this dataset, feature_047 absent is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency, with direction-concordant discovery and validation estimates. The highest-priority unconfirmed result remains H64: feature_047 present versus absent on outcome_008, a post hoc reversed claim with discovery magnitude near the clinical threshold and an interval excluding zero; it should be validated before acceptance. To test whether the emerging feature_047 pattern is isolated or part of a broader marker pattern, I registered four new common-binary main-effect comparisons. Feature_002 and feature_034 are balanced predictors with roughly 1000 observations in each state, providing adequate precision for the approximate 10% thresholds: about 0.0269 for outcome_013 and 0.0282 for outcome_008. I used the same registered convention as the preceding marker panel: the nominal 0/absence-like state is tested for stronger outcome_013 dependency, and the nominal 1/presence-like state is tested for stronger outcome_008 dependency. A positive signed estimate supports the registered direction; a negative signed estimate does not support the registered claim but would motivate a new reversal proposal only if clinically large. These balanced predictors are also useful because they are less dependent on rare marker states and may serve as potential confounders or effect modifiers of the accepted outcome_013 association. I deferred H65 and H66 because they are post hoc feature_047 reversal candidates for the low-mean outcomes outcome_006 and outcome_014. Their point estimates are clinically meaningful relative to those small absolute means, but their intervals are very wide and they compete with H64 for prioritized validation. No causal interpretation or external generalizability is implied.

I selected twelve previously registered comparisons that have no direct evidence yet. The first ten (H73-H82) complete the focused marker-pattern panel built around the accepted outcome_013 feature_047 association and the post hoc outcome_008 feature_047 candidate. For outcome_013, H73/H75/H77/H79/H81 test whether an absent or 0 state of feature_042, feature_021, feature_037, feature_002, or feature_034 is associated with stronger dependency; for outcome_008, H74/H76/H78/H80/H82 test whether a present or 1 state of the same predictors is associated with stronger dependency. These are not causal tests; they test whether the apparent feature_047 pattern is isolated or reproduced by other measured markers. The approximate absolute-mean clinical thresholds are about 0.0269 for outcome_013 and 0.0282 for outcome_008. Because this is a multi-test panel, I will not accept a near-threshold result without a coherent interval and, where useful, independent validation. I also selected H31 and H32 to use the remaining analysis slots productively: they test direct feature_060 main effects within feature_034=1 and feature_034=0 for outcome_006. These were deferred after the feature_060-by-feature_034 interaction H23 failed validation, but the main-effect cells have not been directly tested. The outcome_006 mean is small (about -0.093), so the 10% absolute-mean threshold is only about 0.0093; results should therefore be judged cautiously and preferably with independent validation if strong. I am not rerunning H64-H66 because their comparisons are mathematically equivalent to already tested reversed parents and would not add a new sample. All returned estimates and intervals are already signed to each registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support stronger dependency in the registered exposed/alternative state and negative values do not.

All twelve new discovery results are valid and have adequate cell sizes. Positive signed estimates support the registered direction (stronger dependency in the registered exposed/alternative/absent state), whereas negative signed estimates oppose it. For outcome_013, the clinical threshold is about 0.0269; for outcome_008 it is about 0.0282; for outcome_006 it is about 0.0093. Most marker-panel main effects are null or too weak to prioritize. H73 (R73), H77 (R77), and H79 (R79) are rejected/closed because their entire signed intervals for the claimed direction lie below the relevant clinical threshold. H76 (R76) and H78 (R78) are rejected/closed for the registered present-stronger claim because the positive-signed portions of their intervals are below threshold; their raw opposite signals are not sufficiently supported to override the original hypotheses. H75 (R75), H80 (R80), H81 (R81), and H82 (R82) remain unresolved/deferred because point estimates are below threshold, intervals include zero, and only upper bounds cross the clinical threshold; there is too much uncertainty to accept or validate them now. H74 (R74) is a special case: the registered claim that feature_042 present gives stronger outcome_008 dependency is rejected because the signed estimate is negative and excludes zero. That signed negative result corresponds to a robust raw opposite effect: feature_042 present is associated with a less negative outcome_008 score, with raw magnitude about 0.0295, slightly above threshold. Because this emerged from a multiplicity-prone marker panel, I do not accept the opposite effect now, but I registered a parent-linked reversal proposal so it can be assessed and validated separately. The strongest new result is H31 (R83): feature_060 present versus absent within feature_034=1 has signed estimate +0.0470 (raw stronger dependency by about 0.047), far above the outcome_006 threshold, with a 95% discovery interval excluding zero. However, the lower bound is below the clinical threshold, the result is subgroup-specific, and the corresponding interaction H23 failed independent validation. Therefore H31 remains unresolved/active rather than accepted. H32 (R84), the complement subgroup, is near null but imprecise, so it remains unresolved/deferred. For validation, I request H64: the pre-identified feature_047 present-versus-absent reversal on outcome_008. H64 is simpler than a subgroup main effect, was already the leading unconfirmed candidate, and its discovery interval just excludes zero near the clinical threshold. H31 and the new feature_042 reversal candidate remain active or proposed for subsequent validation if resources remain useful.

The delivered validation evidence closes two post hoc feature_047 candidates. H62 tested whether feature_047 absent versus present was associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency within the feature_060=1 subgroup. Its discovery estimate was positive and significant, but independent validation reversed to a near-zero negative signed estimate (-0.0051; adjusted CI -0.0573 to 0.0471). Thus this subgroup manifestation is not supported. It remains consistent with H37 as a broad main-effect dataset-specific association, but the feature_060 subgroup effect is not robust. H64 tested the reversed feature_047 association on outcome_008: feature_047 present versus absent as stronger dependency. Discovery gave a signed estimate of +0.0282, just reaching the approximate 10% threshold (~0.0282) and excluding zero, but independent validation gave only +0.0056 with an adjusted interval of -0.0355 to +0.0467. The validation point estimate is far below clinical relevance and its uncertainty is compatible with essentially no effect. Combined with the failed validation of the opposite original H57, this indicates that feature_047 present stronger outcome_008 is not robust and should be rejected. Therefore H64 is closed. The supported finding remains only H37: in this dataset, feature_047 absent versus present is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency, with direction-concordant discovery and validation estimates around the clinical threshold, though uncertainty remains substantial. Several feature_047-related follow-ups are now negative, including outcome_012 (H42), outcome_008 (H57/H64), and the feature_060 subgroup of outcome_013 (H62), so H37 appears relatively isolated rather than part of a broad feature_047 pattern. The leading unresolved candidate is H83, the parent-linked reversal for outcome_008 and feature_042: absent versus present with signed discovery +0.0295, CI +0.0055 to +0.0536, around the outcome_008 clinical threshold. Because this emerged from multiplicity-prone marker screening and has not been independently validated, it should not be accepted yet; it is the highest-priority validation candidate. I registered one conditional follow-up test (feature_042 absent versus present among feature_047=1) to assess whether any H83 effect is robust within the large feature_047=1 stratum and potentially less confounded by the accepted feature_047 association. H31 remains a secondary unresolved subgroup candidate for outcome_006, but its corresponding interaction H23 failed validation, so it ranks behind H83. No causal or external-generalizability claim is made.

No assessments are due. The only accepted claim remains H37: in this dataset, feature_047 absent versus present is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency. The leading unresolved dataset-specific candidate is H83, the parent-linked reversal for outcome_008 and feature_042. Its signed discovery estimate is about +0.0295, just above the approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical threshold for outcome_008 (~0.0282), with a 95% discovery interval excluding zero; however, it arose from multiplicity-prone marker screening and has not been independently validated. I therefore register refinements that test whether H83 is robust or driven by measured confounders/effect modifiers. Specifically, I propose feature_042 absent-versus-present tests within the complementary feature_047=0 stratum, within balanced feature_034=1 and feature_034=0 strata, and formal interactions by feature_034 and feature_047. These do not prove causality, but they ask whether the raw direction (feature_042 absent associated with more negative outcome_008) is stable across major strata or appears only in one subgroup. If H83 remains coherent across H84, the feature_047=0 test, and/or feature_034 tests, it will be the strongest candidate for independent validation in a later appraise stage; if it is null or opposite in strata, I will downweight it without validation.

I also register subgroup localizations of the accepted H37 association after H62 failed validation. Feature_060=0 is the complement of the failed feature_060=1 subgroup, and feature_034=0 complements the imprecise positive feature_034=1 subgroup test H61. The registered hypothesis is that feature_047 absent remains associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency in these strata, with expected negative raw exposed-minus-comparator values and hence positive signed estimates. If these follow-ups are broadly consistent, H37 is less likely to be a narrow subgroup artifact; if they are discordant, the accepted main effect remains dataset-specific but heterogeneous. For the active H31 outcome_006 subgroup candidate, I register a smaller test within feature_034=1 and feature_047=1 to see whether the large feature_060-present stronger signal survives in the larger feature_047=1 subgroup. Because H31's corresponding interaction H23 failed validation, this is lower-priority than the H83 robustness program and should not be validated unless the subgroup result remains stable and compelling.

Finally, I add two exploratory feature_055 comparisons because feature_055 level_003 versus level_001 has known adequate cell sizes and provides an independent probe of whether a common categorical marker is associated with either the accepted outcome_013 signal or the candidate outcome_008 signal. These are initially uncertain (anticipated_direction 0), and I will require clinically meaningful point estimates with coherent uncertainty before treating them as meaningful.

No assessments are due. I selected the 11 registered comparisons that currently have no direct evidence: H84 through H94. These are scientifically useful rather than repeat queries. The feature_042/outcome_008 candidate H83 needs robustness screening because it is post hoc and near the approximate clinical threshold (~0.0282). H84 tests whether the absent-versus-present feature_042 contrast remains in the large feature_047=1 stratum, where feature_047 confounding is held constant; H85 tests the complementary feature_047=0 stratum. H86-H87 test whether the candidate effect is consistent across the balanced feature_034 strata. H88 and H89 test formal effect modification by feature_034 and feature_047. For the accepted feature_047/outcome_013 finding, H90 and H91 localize heterogeneity in feature_060=0 and feature_034=0, respectively, because the feature_060=1 subgroup failed validation and the feature_034=1 subgroup was imprecise. H92 probes whether the feature_060/outcome_006 signal in feature_034=1 persists within the large feature_047=1 subgroup. H93 and H94 test feature_055 level_003 versus level_001 for outcome_013 and outcome_008 as an independent categorical marker probe. I did not rerun H83, H31, or H32 because they already have discovery evidence and would not add a new sample.

I assessed all new discovery results with signed estimates interpreted directly in the registered direction. Approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical thresholds are about 0.0282 for outcome_008, 0.0269 for outcome_013, and 0.0093 for outcome_006. For the feature_042/outcome_008 candidate, H84 within the large feature_047=1 stratum gives +0.0311 with a 95% discovery interval excluding zero but with a lower bound below clinical relevance. H86 within feature_034=1 gives +0.0415, also excluding zero but below threshold at the lower bound. These are consistent with the parent main effect H83 (+0.0295) and strengthen the dataset-specific candidate, but they remain post hoc multiplicity-prone refinements, so I keep them unresolved and request independent validation of the main H83 claim rather than accepting on stratum evidence alone. H85 and H87 are in the same direction but point estimates and uncertainty do not support clinically meaningful claims. The interactions H88 and H89 are also imprecise and below clinical relevance. For accepted H37 localizations, H90 within feature_060=0 is near null, while H91 within feature_034=0 is threshold-near but imprecise; I defer these without overturning the accepted main effect. H92 within feature_034=1 and feature_047=1 is strong (+0.0611) and its signed interval lies above the small outcome_006 threshold, but it is a nested subgroup and the corresponding interaction H23 failed validation, so it remains active but unvalidated. The feature_055 outcome_013 probe H93 is null-like and deferred. The registered feature_055 outcome_008 probe H94 is rejected because its significant signed result is opposite the registered direction: it indicates stronger outcome_008 dependency for level_001 versus level_003, not level_003 versus level_001. I registered that reversed comparison as a separate claim for later assessment.

The new validations are decisive and negative for the leading feature_042/outcome_008 candidate. H83 tested feature_042 absent versus present as stronger outcome_008 dependency; its signed discovery estimate was +0.0295, but independent validation was -0.0105 with adjusted interval -0.0458 to +0.0248. That validation is in the opposite direction, includes zero, and is below the approximate outcome_008 clinical threshold near 0.0282. I therefore reject and close H83. The opposite original claim H74 is also not supported: validation gave only +0.0105 with interval -0.0248 to +0.0458, while discovery was significantly opposite. Because the main feature_042/outcome_008 effect failed validation, I close the active stratum refinements H84 and H86 as dataset-specific post hoc leads rather than accepting them. For the response deadlines, H72 validation reversed/nullified the feature_008 present-stronger outcome_008 claim (-0.0256, adjusted CI -0.0730 to +0.0218), and H42 validation showed essentially no feature_047 absent versus present effect on outcome_012 (+0.0001, adjusted CI -0.0303 to +0.0305); both remain rejected and closed. H19, the feature_055 level_003 versus level_001 probe for outcome_010, validated as null (+0.0049, adjusted CI -0.0289 to +0.0387) and is rejected and closed. The supported finding remains only H37: feature_047 absent versus present is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency in this dataset, though its intervals remain uncertain and the association should not be interpreted as causal or externally generalizable. The next most informative candidate is H95, the reversed feature_055 probe for outcome_008: level_001 versus level_003 has signed discovery +0.0315 with 95% discovery interval +0.0018 to +0.0611, just above the clinical threshold, but it was generated after an opposite original H94 probe and has no independent validation. I keep H95 active and plan validation as the priority if it remains useful. I registered feature_034 and feature_047 stratum/effect-modification diagnostics for H95, but the outcome_006 subgroup leads H31/H92 remain secondary because H23 failed validation.

No assessments are due. The only accepted dataset-specific finding remains H37: feature_047 absent versus present is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency, but its subgroup localization is heterogeneous. I therefore register a formal interaction by feature_034 to ask whether the accepted H37 effect is genuinely modified by feature_034 rather than only appearing different in separately estimated subgroups. A clinically meaningful interaction would change the interpretation from a broad but heterogeneous main effect to a stratified association; a near-null or imprecise interaction would support treating subgroup contrasts as descriptive only.

The main unresolved candidate is H95, outcome_008 with feature_055 level_001 versus level_003. Its signed discovery estimate is threshold-near, but it is post hoc because it was registered after the opposite feature_055 probe failed. Before spending another validation slot, I propose level-level refinements. Comparing level_001 with level_002 asks whether level_002 behaves more like the putative stronger-dependency level_001 group or like level_003. Comparing level_002 with level_003 asks whether level_002 sits intermediate between the level_001 and level_003 contrast or is unrelated. Because feature_055 levels are nominal, I do not assume a numeric gradient; the hypotheses are specific group contrasts with plausible null or opposite outcomes. If level_001 versus level_002 and level_002 versus level_003 are coherent with the main contrast, this would strengthen H95 as a validation candidate. If they are discordant, H95 should be downweighted even if the main contrast remains nominally positive.

I also register a formal feature_034 interaction for H95 because H97 separately estimates the feature_034=1 stratum, while the complement is only implicit. This tests whether any level_001-versus-level_003 effect is concentrated in feature_034=1. The corresponding feature_047 interaction was already registered as H99; together these can determine whether H95 is stable or driven by one major stratum.

Finally, I keep the outcome_006 subgroup program as secondary. H92 showed a strong feature_060 present versus absent effect in the nested feature_034=1 and feature_047=1 cell, while H96 remains pending for the feature_047=0 complement. I register a direct interaction by feature_047 within feature_034=1 to test whether the feature_060 association is genuinely concentrated in feature_047=1. This is important because the earlier broader outcome_006 interaction H23 failed validation; a direct positive interaction would be more compelling than nested cell estimates alone, but it still must be treated cautiously because it is subgroup-specific and post hoc.

I am not requesting validation in this explore stage. The next analysis should populate these diagnostics. If H95 diagnostics remain coherent and threshold-near or stronger, H95 should be the next validation target. If they are inconsistent, I will close the feature_055/outcome_008 candidate without validation and redirect to the outcome_006 nested program or accepted-H37 localization only.

No assessments are due in this stage. I am selecting all currently registered claims that still have no direct evidence, plus no previously tested comparison because rerunning existing claims would not add a new discovery sample. The highest-priority set concerns H95, the reversed feature_055 contrast for outcome_008: level_001 versus level_003 has a signed discovery estimate of +0.0315 with 95% interval +0.0018 to +0.0611, threshold-near but clearly post hoc after the opposite H94 probe failed. H100 and H101 test level_001 versus level_002 and level_002 versus level_003. Because feature_055 levels are nominal, these are not assumed to form an ordered gradient; they ask whether the level_003 group is a plausible endpoint or whether the apparent contrast is driven by one arbitrary group split. H97, H98, H99, and H102 test whether H95 is stable across feature_034 and feature_047 strata or is concentrated by strong effect modification. If these diagnostics are coherent and clinically relevant, H95 remains the next validation candidate; if they are discordant or suggest one arbitrary subgroup, I will close the feature_055/outcome_008 program rather than spend a validation slot. The second set, H96 and H103, completes the outcome_006 feature_060 nested program by estimating the feature_047=0 complement and the direct feature_047 interaction within feature_034=1. This is secondary because the broader outcome_006 interaction H23 failed validation, so nested strong subgroup results need direct complement and interaction evidence before they can be trusted. Finally, H104 provides a formal feature_034 interaction for the already accepted H37 feature_047/outcome_013 association, helping determine whether H37's subgroup heterogeneity reflects true effect modification or merely imprecise subgroup estimates. I do not request validation in this analyze stage; validation will be decided after appraisal of these discovery diagnostics.

I assessed the new discovery evidence using signed estimates interpreted directly in the registered direction. For reference, approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical thresholds are about 0.0282 for outcome_008, 0.0269 for outcome_013, and 0.0093 for outcome_006. H100 tests level_001 versus level_002 for outcome_008 and gives a near-null signed estimate (-0.0006; 95% discovery interval -0.0320 to +0.0307). I reject and close this specific level_001-versus-level_002 claim. However, H101 tests level_002 versus level_003 and gives +0.0321 (95% interval +0.0014 to +0.0628), a threshold-near positive effect. Together with the main H95 estimate of +0.0315 and H100's null between level_001 and level_002, the data suggest a plausible nominal-group pattern in which level_001 and level_002 behave similarly and are more strongly associated with outcome_008 dependency than level_003. This coherence makes H95 worth independent validation, but it does not justify accepting H95 or H101 yet: the main interval lower bound is below clinical relevance, H95 is a reversed post hoc probe after H94, and multiple feature_055 level contrasts were examined. H101 is therefore kept active but unresolved as a competing or supporting nominal contrast.

The feature_034 diagnostics do not argue against H95. H97, within feature_034=1, gives +0.0278 (interval -0.0118 to +0.0675), near but just below the outcome_008 threshold. H102, the formal feature_034 interaction, is near null (-0.0081; interval -0.0675 to +0.0514). I reject and close H102 as unsupported effect modification, and defer H97 because the stratum estimate is imprecise. These results indicate that the feature_055 outcome_008 signal is not obviously created by feature_034 effect modification. The feature_047 diagnostics are more cautionary but not decisive. H98, within the large feature_047=1 stratum, gives +0.0268 (interval -0.0066 to +0.0601), just below threshold and imprecise. H99, the formal feature_047 interaction, is negative in the registered signed scale and very imprecise (-0.0230; interval -0.0960 to +0.0500). I close H99 unresolved because it does not support a clinically meaningful feature_047 interaction and I do not want to spend validation on it, but I do not treat it as proof that feature_047 is irrelevant. Overall, H95 remains the leading dataset-specific candidate because its main estimate is threshold-near and the level coherence is plausible, but it needs independent validation before acceptance.

For outcome_006, H96 estimates feature_060 present versus absent in the feature_047=0 complement of the earlier positive feature_047=1 nested cell. The signed estimate is -0.0152 (interval -0.1223 to +0.0920), opposite to the claimed direction and very imprecise in only 95 versus 95 observations. I reject and close H96. H103, the direct feature_047 interaction within feature_034=1, gives +0.0763 (interval -0.0417 to +0.1942). Although the point estimate is large, the interval is far too wide and the complement estimate from H96 is discordant; combined with the prior validation failure of H23, this closes the outcome_006 subgroup program as insufficiently supported. For the accepted H37 feature_047/outcome_013 association, H104 provides the formal feature_034 interaction: -0.0053 (interval -0.0592 to +0.0486), near null. I reject and close it as unsupported modification, supporting interpretation of H37 as a broad dataset-specific association rather than a claim of feature_034 stratification. I request validation for H95 because it is the most informative eligible unresolved candidate; independent validation will test reproducibility in the supplied dataset framework without implying causality or external generalizability.

The new validation for H95 resolves the leading feature_055/outcome_008 candidate negatively. Approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical thresholds are about 0.0282 for outcome_008, 0.0269 for outcome_013, and 0.0093 for outcome_006. H95 (outcome_008, feature_055 level_001 versus level_003, registered direction -1) had signed discovery +0.0315 with 95% discovery interval +0.0018 to +0.0611. Its independent validation was only +0.0057, adjusted interval -0.0403 to +0.0517. The validation point is far below the clinical threshold and the interval includes both null and clinically meaningful values, with no reproducible signal. Because H95 was a post hoc reversal after the opposite H94 probe and the validation is incompatible with the discovery magnitude, I reject and close H95. The related level_002 versus level_003 discovery, H101, remains threshold-near but is now closed unresolved rather than promoted: H100 level_001 versus level_002 was null, the H95 sibling validation failed, and no independent validation of H101 exists. Similarly, feature_034 and feature_047 stratum diagnostics for H95 (H97, H98) are imprecise and no longer worth keeping active; their interactions were not supportive. Thus the feature_055/outcome_008 program is treated as unsupported after validation.

For response deadline H64, the reversed feature_047 contrast for outcome_008 (present versus absent) had discovery +0.0282 with interval +0.0019 to +0.0546, but independent validation was +0.0056 with adjusted interval -0.0355 to +0.0467. The validation is too small and imprecise to support a clinically meaningful outcome_008 association. I keep H64 rejected and closed. This confirms that feature_047's supported association is not a broad outcome_008 effect.

The earlier outcome_006 feature_060 subgroup leads are also closed without acceptance. H31 and H92 had positive nested discovery estimates, but the broader feature_034 interaction H23 failed validation, the feature_047=0 complement H96 was discordant and imprecise, and direct interaction H103 was too imprecise. These remain unresolved leads rather than accepted findings. The only accepted dataset-specific claim remains H37: feature_047 absent versus present is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency. The formal feature_034 interaction H104 was near null, so H37 is best interpreted as a broad dataset-specific association, not a claim of feature_034 stratification, causality, or external generalizability.

With the feature_042, feature_008, feature_047, feature_055, and feature_060/outcome_006 programs now closed or unsupported, the most informative next step is broad discovery on outcome_006 for untested common binary/categorical predictors. Outcome_006 has a smaller clinical threshold and remains relatively untested compared with outcome_008 and outcome_013. I registered twelve outcome_006 main-effect hypotheses spanning feature_042, feature_045, feature_021, feature_012, feature_037, feature_050, feature_020, feature_052, feature_065, feature_011, feature_054, and feature_063. Future validation should be reserved for a candidate that is discovery-significant, clearly above the outcome_006 threshold, and conceptually coherent, rather than spent on H101 or previously failed programs.

No assessments are due, so this stage only registers new scientifically useful comparisons. The current accepted dataset-specific finding remains H37: feature_047 absent versus present is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency. The formal feature_034 interaction was null, so the main unresolved issue for H37 is not whether feature_034 modifies it, but whether the broad association may nevertheless be effect-modified by other plausible binary markers that showed heterogeneous subgroup estimates, especially feature_060 and feature_002. I register formal interactions for the accepted feature_047/outcome_013 comparison in feature_060=1 and feature_002=1 versus their complements. A clinically meaningful interaction would justify refining H37 into a stratified dataset-specific association; a near-null or imprecise interaction would support treating subgroup contrasts as descriptive only and retaining the broad interpretation.

For new discovery allocation, I prioritize two relatively undertested outcome scales. Outcome_014 has an approximately 10% mean-scale clinical threshold near 0.0093 and has only a few tested predictors, making it attractive for focused follow-up. I selected predictors with prior threshold-near or unresolved signals across other dependency scores: feature_002 present versus absent, because prior outcome_008 evidence pointed mildly toward present having lower scores; feature_042 absent versus present, because prior outcome_008 stratum signals were in the absent-stronger direction before main validation failure; feature_021 and feature_050 absent versus present, because they had weak unresolved contrasts on outcome_013; and feature_055 level_001 versus level_003 and level_002 versus level_003, because feature_055 levels were an important unresolved nominal-group pattern on outcome_008 and could differ on outcome_014. I also add feature_030 absent versus present as a common untested binary predictor to broaden coverage of the outcome_014 predictor set.

For outcome_006, H105-H116 already register a broad main-effect panel. I add feature_002 present versus absent, feature_008 absent versus present, and feature_023 absent versus present to cover common predictors that were not in that panel and had prior evidence suggestive enough to be worth screening. Outcome_006 also has a low clinical threshold, so high-prevalence contrasts can identify modest but meaningful associations. These proposals are all exploratory dataset-specific comparisons; none asserts causality or external generalizability. Future validation should be reserved for candidates that are discovery-significant, clearly above their outcome-specific threshold, and supported by coherent stratum or level diagnostics rather than isolated nominal group comparisons.

No assessments are due. I am requesting 12 previously registered analyses with no current direct evidence, prioritizing new data over reruns. First, I keep two H37 localization diagnostics: H117 and H118 formally test whether the accepted feature_047/outcome_013 association is modified by feature_060 or feature_002. H104 already showed no feature_034 modification, but feature_060 and feature_002 had heterogeneous subgroup estimates. A clinically meaningful positive interaction would support refining H37 into a stratified dataset-specific association; a near-null or imprecise interaction would support the broad interpretation already suggested by H104. Second, I prioritize outcome_014 because it is relatively undertested and has an approximately 10% absolute-mean clinical threshold near 0.0093. I select H119 feature_002 present versus absent, H120 feature_042 absent versus present, H121 feature_021 absent versus present, and the nominal feature_055 contrasts H123 level_001 versus level_003 and H124 level_002 versus level_003. These are outcome-specific tests, not a claim that the failed feature_055/outcome_008 program transfers to outcome_014. Third, I partially complete the outcome_006 discovery panel with H105 feature_042, H106 feature_045, H107 feature_021, H110 feature_050, and H126 feature_002, choosing predictors that either have prior threshold-near or unresolved signals or are common enough to provide a useful screen. I defer H122 feature_050 for outcome_014, H125 feature_030, H127 feature_008, and H128 feature_023 because current capacity is better used on cross-outcome coherence for feature_042, feature_021, and feature_002, plus the formal H37 localization tests. No validation is requested at this stage; appraise will decide whether any discovery result is sufficiently strong, above the relevant clinical threshold, and coherent across components or strata to merit one of the remaining validation slots.

I assessed the newly delivered discovery evidence using the signed estimates already oriented to the registered claim direction. Approximate 10%-of-mean clinical thresholds are about 0.027 for outcome_013 and about 0.009 for outcome_006 and outcome_014. For the accepted H37 localization tests, H117 gives a formal feature_060 interaction of +0.046 with a wide interval crossing zero (-0.008 to +0.100). Although the point estimate is threshold-near, it is not statistically established, and the earlier feature_060 subgroup estimate for H37 failed independent validation (H62); therefore I reject the claim of feature_060 modification and close it. H118 gives a near-null feature_002 interaction (-0.006; interval -0.060 to +0.048), also unsupported. Together with the null feature_034 interaction H104, these results support interpreting H37 as a broad dataset-specific association rather than an effect-modified or stratified association. For outcome_014, H119 is near null and rejected. H123 and H124 are small and imprecise feature_055 nominal-level contrasts and are rejected as unsupported. H120 and H121 have threshold-near point estimates but 95% intervals that include zero and clinically irrelevant values, so they are deferred rather than promoted. For outcome_006, H105 and H126 are below or indistinguishable from the clinical threshold and are rejected. H106 and H110 have suggestive threshold-exceeding point estimates but imprecise intervals that include null and subthreshold effects, so they remain unresolved and deferred. The key result is H107: outcome_006, feature_021 absent versus present, has a signed estimate +0.802 with interval +0.782 to +0.822, an enormous effect far above the clinical threshold and statistically precise. Given its magnitude, however, I audit it cautiously: it may reflect a genuine strong predictor-association in this dataset, but it could also reflect a coding, batch-like, or technical subgroup artifact, especially because feature_021 had only weak signals on other outcomes. I therefore do not accept it on discovery evidence alone. I request independent validation of H107. If validation reproduces an effect clearly above threshold, I would accept a dataset-specific association with explicit noncausal and non-generalizable caveats; if validation is discordant, the feature_021/outcome_006 signal should be closed as unsupported or artifactual.

H107 is now a strong accepted dataset-specific finding. The original discovery was outcome_006 feature_021 absent versus present with signed estimate +0.802 (95% CI +0.782 to +0.822), and the independent validation reproduced it almost exactly: signed estimate +0.811 with adjusted interval +0.782 to +0.841. Both estimates are many times larger than the approximate outcome_006 clinical threshold near 0.0093, and both intervals are far above null. I therefore accept H107 as a dataset-specific association of feature_021 absence/presence with markedly stronger outcome_006 dependency in the registered direction. Because validation is independent but still within this dataset framework, this acceptance is not a causal or external-generalizability claim. I will continue to characterize the association through stratum and interaction checks to ensure the magnitude is not concentrated in one implausible technical subgroup. H83 remains rejected: the original discovery for feature_042 absent versus present on outcome_008 was +0.0295, but validation was opposite and imprecise (-0.0105, adjusted CI -0.0458 to +0.0248), so the claim is not reproducible. H19 remains rejected: feature_055 level_003 versus level_001 on outcome_010 had small discovery +0.0065 and validation +0.0049 with adjusted CI including null and subthreshold values. The most informative next step is to complete the outcome_006 panel and examine whether the enormous H107 effect is stable across feature_034, feature_047, feature_060, and feature_002 strata or is confined to one subgroup.

No assessments are due, so this stage registers new comparisons. The two active dataset-specific accepted findings are H37 and H107. H37 is the accepted feature_047 absent-versus-present association with stronger outcome_013 dependency, broad after null feature_034, feature_060, and feature_002 interaction probes. H107 is the very large, independently validated outcome_006 feature_021 absent-versus-present association, signed +0.802 in discovery and +0.811 in validation, far above the approximate outcome_006 clinical threshold around 0.009. Before spending validation slots on weaker candidates, I propose scientifically useful audits and follow-ups. First, feature_064 has a summary distribution almost identical to feature_047, so I test feature_064 absent versus present on outcome_013, outcome_006, and outcome_014. If feature_064 replicates H37 on outcome_013 and mirrors feature_047-related contrasts elsewhere, the accepted feature_047 signal may be partly a duplicate-marker or coding artifact; if it does not replicate, feature_047 is more likely to be a distinct measured label. Second, because H107 is extremely large, I test whether it persists in clinically relevant extremes of feature_061, a partially observed numeric predictor with age-like distribution: low feature_061 <=45 and high feature_061 >=65. A robust large signed effect across these strata would support interpreting H107 as a broad outcome_006-specific association rather than an artifact confined to a covariate range. If the effect collapses in one stratum, the accepted claim should be narrowed or strongly caveated. Third, I test whether H107 is outcome-specific by repeating feature_021 absent versus present on outcome_001 and outcome_012. I expect these to be far weaker than outcome_006; a similarly large effect would indicate a more general technical or biological marker pattern and would change interpretation. Fourth, I register a formal H37-by-feature_021 interaction to test whether the accepted feature_047/outcome_013 association is modified by the H107 marker. A null or small interaction would reinforce H37 as broad; a large interaction would suggest the accepted H37 should be refined by feature_021 strata. Finally, feature_001 and feature_046 have identical marginal summaries and are untested for outcome_006, so I register both present-versus-absent contrasts to screen whether either contains a signal and to check for duplicate-marker effects. All proposals remain exploratory dataset-specific associations; none asserts causality or external generalizability.

No assessments are due. I request 12 untested comparisons focused on the two accepted dataset-specific findings. H107 has an enormous signed discovery/validation effect for outcome_006 with feature_021 absent versus present, so I test whether this is stable or subgroup-concentrated. H131 and H134 are formal interaction tests of feature_034 and feature_047 modification; H129/H130 and H132/H133 give stratum-specific signed magnitudes; H135/H136 extend the same check to the common binary feature_060. A consistent large signed effect with near-null interactions would support a broad dataset-specific association, while a very large complement-stratum contrast or interaction would suggest narrowing.
